title: What if my debt is forgiven? | Internal Revenue Service
text: Skip to main content What if my debt is forgiven? More In News Working Families Tax Cuts News releases Tax relief in disaster situations Topics in the news Fact sheets IRS statements and announcements IRS Tax Tips IRS guidance Multimedia center Tax articles to share Posters to share The tax impact of debt forgiveness or cancellation depends on your individual facts and circumstances. Generally, if you borrow money from a commercial lender and the lender later cancels or forgives the debt, you may have to include the cancelled amount in income for tax purposes. The lender is usually required to report the amount of the canceled debt to you and the IRS on a Form 1099-C, Cancellation of Debt (Info Copy Only) PDF . There are several exceptions to the taxability of cancelled debt, such as insolvency or bankruptcy. Related Topic no. 431, Canceled debt – Is it taxable or not?
